doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Fats Waller and the song Nobody Knows
summary: Carter met Waller in the late twenties, recorded with him with McKinney's, and finished Waller's song with lyricist Bud Allen.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: While we’re discussing these Harlem stride players, maybe we could go through several of them that I happened to just job down that you could give us your impressions of or reminiscences about. We mentioned Willy “The Lion” and his relationship to you. Fats Waller, you just brought up, and when did you get to know him?

Gee, I don’t know exactly, but just being around Harlem at the time. Oh, let’s see, it was probably the late twenties, maybe in the mid . . . late twenties, I would say. Then we recorded together for the McKinney’s Cotton Pickers, you know, the thing with Don Redmond, and . . .
Other than that, I don’t think we ever played together.
That tune that you collaborated on, which was . . . as early as 1927 that was published, I think, Nobody Knows.
Oh, that’s right, Nobody . . . see, I’d forgotten that.
Gee, I . . . who was the lyric writer on that? I’ve forgotten his name.
That’s a good question. I forgot his name, also.

Buddy somebody, was it? But, oh, boy, I’ve forgotten his name, and I can see his face before me, too. But anyway, yeah, Fats had this tune, but he didn’t have it completed, and he asked me to work on it with him, and that’s how it came about. Yes, I’d forgotten that, but that’s . . . gee, that’s so long ago, in addition to which, I don’t even know how the song goes now. I haven’t a copy of it.
So he must have known you then, that early, if he . . .
Yes, yes, of course he did.
. . . if he asked you for help on that.
Yeah, well, he probably wasn’t that much older than I was. Gee, Fats Waller, huh?

Bud Allen, that’s right. Gee whiz, yes, Bud Allen. I wonder what ever became of Bud Allen. I used to see him around Harlem now and then, but I didn’t know what he was into, and I don’t know any other song to which he wrote the lyrics. So that part of my memory is a little clouded.
